beatOutlines.textOutline: Traditional envelopes place fixed percentage bands, like 3% or 5%, above and below the moving average.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: John Bollinger integrated statistical standard deviation, allowing the bands to breathe with volatility.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In rangebound markets, the lower band provides support while the upper band acts as a natural target.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Yet in strong trends price walks the upper band; shorting merely because it touches the band is a fatal error.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The Band Width indicator measures band dispersion; its historical lows pre-warn of a major imminent breakout.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Many technical analysts abandon arbitrary numbers in favor of the Fibonacci sequence for moving averages.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The 8, 13, and 21-day averages capture short-term momentum and pullback entries with organic precision.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy notes Fibonacci periods harmonize with market cycles, clustering institutional orders at key curves.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Richard Donchian's 4-Week breakout rule became the backbone of systematic trading and the Turtle Traders.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: This rule leaves zero room for subjective bias: when the 4-week high breaks, you buy without hesitation.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Tinkering with backtest software parameters leads traders to mistake past noise for a future formula.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Yet the moment unseen live market data arrives, that so-called perfect system instantly blows up.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Perry Kaufman solved the rigid parameter dilemma: a moving average that automatically adapts to market speed.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When the market goes sideways KAMA goes entirely flat, neutralizing wasteful whipsaws completely.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: Percentage Envelopes use fixed bands; Bollinger Bands dynamically adapt using 2σ
In trading ranges, Bollinger Bands provide reliable overbought/oversold targets
In runaway trends, prices walk the outer band—touching it is NOT an auto-sell
Bollinger Band Width contraction ('The Squeeze') warns of impending volatility explosion
Fibonacci MAs (8, 13, 21, 55, 89) align periods with organic market cycles
Donchian's 4-Week Rule serves as the time-tested foundation of mechanical trend following
Over-optimization leads to curve-fitting; past perfection guarantees live failure
Kaufman's KAMA dynamically speeds up during trends and halts flat during sideways chop
bottomTakeaway: Discipline and grounded market understanding are essential for survival.
